observables.name: ac_dc_not_shared
observables.target: the full run of the cable rack
observables.method: Show the rack carries AC or DC power cabling, not both.
observables.accepts: no rack carries both AC and DC power cabling

citation_span: AC and DC power cabling shall not be run on the same cable rack.

observables.name: grounding_leads_off_power_rack
observables.method: Show no grounding lead shares the rack with power cable.
observables.accepts: no grounding lead is run on a rack carrying power cable

citation_span: Grounding leads are not battery return leads, and shall not be run on the cable rack with power cable.

observables.name: cable_flows_over_rack_edge
observables.target: where the cable leaves the rack
observables.method: Show the cable passing over the rack edge, not through it.
observables.accepts: the cable flows over the edge of the rack, not through it

citation_span: Cable must flow over the edge of the cable rack, not through the cable rack.

observables.name: unsupported_span_under_2ft
observables.target: the unsupported run between rack and equipment
observables.method: Measure the longest unsupported span where the cable leaves the rack.
observables.accepts: the unsupported span is 2 feet or less

citation_span: shall not be unsupported for a distance greater than two (2) feet for cables 1/0 and smaller
notes: Threshold is gauge-dependent; the 2/0-and-larger case is H.10.7b. Split so the applicable limit is unambiguous per cable.

observables.name: unsupported_span_under_3ft
observables.target: the unsupported run between rack and equipment
observables.method: Measure the longest unsupported span. Horizontal support allows only 18 inches.
observables.accepts: the unsupported span is 3 feet or less, or 18 inches where horizontally supported

citation_span: Cables 2/0 and larger shall not be unsupported for a distance greater than three (3) feet (18 inches for horizontal support)
notes: The parenthetical 18-inch horizontal limit is folded into the acceptance criterion rather than split again, because the two cases share one measurement.

observables.name: secured_with_12_waxed_lacing
observables.target: the securing points along the cable
observables.method: Show the cable secured with #12 waxed lacing cord and correct stitching.
observables.accepts: the cable is secured with #12 waxed lacing cord using the specified stitching and knots

citation_span: Power cables shall be secured using #12 waxed lacing cord and the appropriate stitching and knots.

observables.name: exposed_end_taped_and_capped
observables.method: Show the end insulated with tape and a heat shrink cap.
observables.accepts: the exposed end carries both tape and a heat shrink cap

citation_span: Exposed ends of power cable shall be insulated with tape and heat shrink caps.
notes: Applies only where an exposed end exists, so a fully terminated cable is not in force.

observables.name: label_top_center_front
observables.target: the top center of the bay, front
observables.method: Photograph the front top center label.
observables.accepts: a label is fitted at the top center of the front

observables.name: label_top_center_rear
observables.target: the top center of the bay, rear
observables.method: Photograph the rear top center label.
observables.accepts: a label is fitted at the top center of the rear

observables.name: letter_height_half_inch
observables.method: Measure the character height on the label.
observables.accepts: characters are 1/2 inch high and black

citation_span: Rectifier cabinets and Power Distribution Bays shall be labeled on the top center, both front and rear, with black
notes: Letter height is a measurement, not something a photograph settles on its own.

observables.name: circuit_labelled
observables.target: the fuse block, fuse panel or circuit breaker
observables.accepts: the distribution circuit carries an identification label

citation_span: All distribution circuits shall be labeled, including fuse blocks, fuse panels, and circuit breakers.
